title: AI labs are now spending more compute teaching models to think than to learn
key_facts: The article argues that frontier AI labs are putting more compute into post-training (teaching a model to reason) and inference-time reasoning, not only into ever-larger pretraining runs.
Its standfirst says Epoch AI data shows post-training compute overtook pretraining in early 2026, but the body does not present that data.
The body cites an Epoch AI analysis estimating that GPT-5 (August 2025) used less training compute than GPT-4.5, and says public evidence does not reveal the full training budgets of either model.
It traces the shift to reinforcement-learning-on-reasoning techniques published from September 2024, and to DeepSeek's R1 in January 2025, after which most major labs shipped reasoning variants.
It says industry estimates put reasoning models at 10 to 100 times more tokens per query than non-reasoning models, so inference compute is used every time a user asks something.

It ties this to Micron's record fiscal fourth-quarter revenue of $54.23 billion (announced 30 Sep) and TrendForce's estimate that the nine biggest cloud providers will spend over $886.7 billion in 2026.
The author presents these links as interpretation ('Frankly, this reframes...') and adds that pretraining does not disappear.
quote_evidence: Public evidence still does not reveal the full training budgets for either model, but the direction is clear: the new performance gains are coming from a mix of pretraining, post-training and inference-time reasoning rather than a simple bigger-pretraining-run story.
None of this means pretraining disappears. Someone still has to build the base model those reasoning techniques get bolted onto.
Frankly, this reframes the entire AI capex argument that bond investors and chip analysts keep having.
why_it_matters_hint: If true, AI chip and memory demand would depend more on running reasoning models than on training bigger ones, but the article's own evidence is partial.
event_date: Article dated 11 Oct 2026; the trend it describes dates from Sep 2024 to 2025
notes: Read Startup Fortune in full. An analysis and opinion piece, not new reporting. Headline and standfirst state a crossover as fact that the body does not support with data. Sections about Micron's venture fund and a looped transformer paper are unrelated inserts and were not used.
